Article Title: Reliance shares surge almost 12%, see best single-day gain in over 6 years: What's driving the rally
Article Text:
Reliance shares climbed to Rs 1,237.45 on the BSE, up 6.35 per cent at 10:22 am on Monday.

According to Google Trends, searches for ‘reliance share price’ surged by over 5,000% in India.

RIL share price today: Reliance Industries shares witnessed a sharp rally on Monday, climbing almost 12 per cent in their strongest single-day performance since April 7, 2020. The surge came after the company announced its highest-ever quarterly profit of Rs 29,550 crore for the July-September period.On the BSE, the stock advanced 11.64 per cent to close at its intraday peak of Rs 1,299. A similar rally was seen on the NSE, where the shares gained 11.59 per cent to finish at Rs 1,300, also the day's highest level.The sharp rise in the stock added Rs 1,83,298.24 crore to the company's market capitalisation, taking its total valuation to Rs 17,57,876.78 crore.Reliance Industries, which holds the position of India's most valuable listed company by market capitalisation, emerged as the top-performing stock among the Sensex and Nifty constituents. Its gains also provided a significant lift to the broader equity market.The benchmark indices extended their winning run to a third consecutive session. The BSE Sensex, comprising 30 stocks, advanced 1,233.25 points, or 1.66 per cent, to finish at its day's high of 75,692.78. The NSE Nifty, with 50 constituents, climbed 387.70 points, or 1.68 per cent, to settle at 23,440.80, also its highest level during the session.The rally followed Reliance Industries Ltd's announcement on Friday that its consolidated profit for July-September had touched a record Rs 29,550 crore. This represented a 33.8 per cent increase over the corresponding period of the previous year. Stronger earnings from its oil-to-chemicals business, supported by higher global fuel margins, along with expansion in the telecom business, helped compensate for the relatively weaker performance of its retail operations.In the July-September quarter of the previous year, profit after tax, including the share of associates and joint ventures, stood at Rs 22,092 crore. Meanwhile, net profit attributable to the company's owners increased 40 per cent to Rs 25,548 crore.Consolidated revenue for the latest quarter grew 27.8 per cent to Rs 3,62,268 crore. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) also registered a 23.9 per cent rise, reaching an all-time high of Rs 62,409 crore.The July-September earnings were also higher than the Rs 23,196 crore profit recorded in the preceding quarter, marking a new quarterly record for India's largest listed company by market capitalisation.A major contributor to the improved performance was the recovery in Reliance's oil-to-chemicals (O2C) operations. Higher transportation fuel cracks and better petrochemical margins strengthened profitability in this segment. The digital services business also reported growth, helping support overall earnings, although the retail division remained relatively weak.Among the company's businesses, O2C, which includes its oil refining and petrochemical operations, accounted for the largest share of the growth. Its EBITDA increased 67.9 per cent to Rs 25,203 crore, while revenue from the segment rose 44.2 per cent to Rs 2,31,601 crore.Jefferies said O2C “hit the bullseye”, citing record crude processing, flexible sourcing and a shift towards higher-value fuel exports that helped Reliance benefit from favourable refining conditions. The brokerage raised its earnings forecasts following the stronger-than-expected results.Emkay Global also pointed to the sharp recovery in O2C and improving profitability at Jio as key drivers of the earnings beat. It raised its estimates and maintained that the stock's valuation remained attractive.Retail continued to be the softer part of the business. Reliance Retail's gross revenue rose 6.4 per cent to Rs 91,716 crore, but EBITDA before a one-time impairment charge declined 8.6 per cent to Rs 6,228 crore. Investments in digital commerce, higher input costs and the shift of major festivals to the December quarter weighed on performance. JioMart, however, recorded 42 per cent revenue growth.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market and other asset classes given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)
Article Summary: Reliance shares climbed to Rs 1,237.45 on the BSE, up 6.35 per cent at 10:22 am on Monday. Google Trends, searches for ‘reliance share price’ surged by over 5,000% in India.

Article Title: India among world's best-performing markets in October as investors rotate away from AI stocks: Goldman Sachs
Article Text:
AI-linked stocks trail as IT services power India's October rally

Indian equities were reportedly among the world's best-performing markets in October, outperforming the broader Asia-Pacific region as investors shifted money away from AI-sensitive technology stocks and towards other sectors. The trend was also visible within India, where IT services stocks gained ground while companies linked to the AI ecosystem lagged, according to a Goldman Sachs Research report.The Nifty outperformed the broader Asia-Pacific region excluding Japan (MXAPJ) by 7 percentage points, reversing its underperformance during the first nine months of 2026.The change in investor preference was particularly sharp within India's technology space. Stocks classified as AI enablers, which had beaten the Nifty by 76 percentage points between January and September, underperformed the benchmark by 6 percentage points in October. IT services companies moved in the opposite direction, outperforming the index by 14 percentage points to become the month's leading sector.Goldman Sachs attributed India's gains to a broader shift in global portfolios. “India benefited from market rotation away from AI-sensitive North Asian markets,” the report said, describing the country as one of the world's best-performing markets in October, as cited by ANI.The recovery followed a difficult third quarter, when the Nifty had fallen 10 per cent from its peak to its trough. It recovered 3 per cent from its early-October low. Momentum continued in the week ended October 30, with the benchmark gaining 2 per cent against a 1 per cent rise in MXAPJ.The latest advance was not limited to large-cap stocks. Mid-cap and small-cap shares rose 3-4 per cent during the week, while pharmaceuticals gained 7 per cent. Financial stocks were relatively subdued, advancing just 1 per cent.Institutional flows also showed signs of improvement. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought $1.2 billion worth of Indian equities during the week, although their net outflows for 2026 remained high at $31 billion. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) added $400 million, taking their purchases for the year to $75 billion.Earnings have provided another source of support. Companies accounting for 58 per cent of the MSCI India index's market capitalisation had reported their July-September results by the time of the report. Their combined profits were tracking 15 per cent higher than a year earlier and 13 per cent above the previous quarter.The performance, however, was uneven. Metals and mining, utilities and healthcare companies delivered more positive surprises, while cement and materials and consumer discretionary firms reported more earnings misses.The rally has also made Indian equities expensive relative to regional peers. The market's forward price-to-earnings ratio stood at 18.4 times, while its valuation premium over the broader Asia-Pacific region reached 92 per cent, close to historical highs.With several large companies due to announce results in early November, investors will be looking for earnings to justify the market's elevated valuations.
Article Summary: Indian equities were reportedly among the world's best-performing markets in October. Investors shifted money away from AI-sensitive technology stocks and towards other sectors. The trend was also visible within India, where IT services stocks gained ground while companies linked to the AI ecosystem lagged, according to a Goldman Sachs Research report.

Article Title: Stock market today: BSE Sensex ends over 1,200 points up, Nifty50 crosses 23,800; top 5 reasons for rally
Article Text:
Jefferies said a potential reduction in LTCG tax could encourage foreign investors to return to the Indian market, which they have been steadily moving away from.

Why did the stock market rise today? Top reasons

Expectations of an LTCG tax review gather momentum

Oil prices

AI-related trade loses momentum

Foreign investor buying provides support

Rupee strengthens against the dollar

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Stock market rally today: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 continued their winning on Tuesday after the stock market hit a 7-week closing high in the previous session. Softer oil prices, rising expectations of a possible review of the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax structure and other supportive factors lifted investor confidence, leading to both major indices rallying over 1%.BSE Sensex ended the day at 76,917.85, up 1,225 points or 1.62%. Nifty50 closed at 23,810.85, up 370 points or 1.58%. The rally added nearly Rs 4 lakh crore to the combined market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE, taking the total to Rs 486 lakh crore.IndiGo and HDFC Bank led the Sensex gainers, with both stocks advancing around 3%. UltraTech Cement, Hindustan Unilever (HUL), Asian Paints, Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Finserv and Infosys also rose by approximately 2% each.Reliance Industries was among the notable laggards, declining a little over 1% after recording a historic 12% jump in the previous session.V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited says that circumstances are ideal for the continuation of the ongoing market rally.“Decline in Brent crude to $104, further weakening of the AI trade, continuing flow of good Q2 results and FIIs turning buyers have potential to accelerate the ongoing rally.The 11.6% surge in a mega cap stock in one day is very rare. But this happened in RIL yesterday. Huge delivery based buying of around Rs 6413 crores, supported by excellent Q2 results, triggered massive short covering in the stock. Massive value buying along with big short covering leads to such sharp surges in stocks, even in megacaps. The takeaway from this experience is that patient value buying will be rewarded. It is possible that there are short positions in many quality large-caps. These are short-positions created by bears on expectations of continued FII selling. The circumstances are changing,” he says.“While the AI trade has slightly weakened, it is important to understand that this is only a correction, not yet a crash. Results of many AI companies continue to be good. So watch out for the trends in this segment. Results of the US mid-term elections due tomorrow and its impact on geopolitical dynamics will be keenly watched by the market in the coming days,” he adds.Hopes of a possible change in the taxation of equity capital gains gained traction after Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday that the government would "consider" foreign investors' request for a review of the tax structure."The circumstances have changed and, therefore, the voices of concern are louder,'' she said at a media event, referring to reports that her administration had received suggestions to reconsider the levies on long-term capital gains (LTCG) for overseas investors."I quite appreciate that. So, I'll consider all this... Our growth is very important; where people are putting their very best, we are able to see sustained 7(%)-plus growth.''In a recent report, Jefferies said a potential reduction in LTCG tax could encourage foreign investors to return to the Indian market, which they have been steadily moving away from.Crude oil prices edged up marginally on Tuesday morning but continued to trade significantly below the levels of around $110 per barrel recorded in recent weeks. Brent crude futures stayed below $105 per barrel, while WTI crude futures remained under $97 per barrel.Apple announced its July-September quarter results on Monday, reporting earnings that exceeded expectations. The iPhone maker recorded a "revenue record", supported by sales of iPhones and growth in services revenue. However, higher expenses associated with artificial intelligence have raised concerns about pressure on profit margins.Apple CFO Kevan Parekh cautioned that gross margins in the final part of the year would moderate slightly from the 47.9% reported for the September quarter."We expect gross margin to be between 45% and 46%. This includes primarily the impact of higher memory costs, as well as some costs related to the ramp of Siri AI," Parekh said.Indian equities, meanwhile, are increasingly being viewed as an ‘Anti-AI’ trade. Consequently, concerns that the AI-driven market frenzy could lose steam are often seen as a positive for Dalal Street.Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) continued to purchase Indian equities on Monday, recording net buying of nearly Rs 3,115 crore, according to provisional NSE data. The buying follows a period of heavy selling that had unsettled the domestic market.FIIs were net sellers through September and the first half of October. The trend reversed in the latter half of October, with foreign investors returning to buying. Their purchases have continued into November, offering some relief to market bulls.The rupee opened 0.26% higher at 94.6550 against the US dollar on Tuesday, compared with its previous close of 94.90.Commenting on the currency's outlook, Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst of Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities, said, “With the US election date approaching, markets will closely monitor whether the administration maintains this diplomatic stance or geopolitical tensions resurface. Lower crude prices could provide near-term support to the domestic currency. The rupee is expected to trade in a range of 94.50–95.25. "
Article Summary: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 continued winning on Tuesday after the stock market hit a 7-week closing high in the previous session. Softer oil prices, rising expectations of a possible review of the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax structure and other supportive factors lifted investor confidence, leading to both major indices rallying over 1%.

Article Title: 'We will navigate through challenges': IndiGo CEO Willie Walsh on airline industry's tough phase
Article Text:
IndiGo sees growth potential despite industry headwinds, focuses on cost control

IndiGo focuses on costs amid elevated fuel expenses

A350 deliveries and Navi Mumbai airport plans

IndiGo sees significant growth opportunities despite rising fuel costs and other pressures facing the aviation industry, CEO Willie Walsh said on Monday, adding that the airline would focus on maintaining a competitive cost base while navigating the challenges.At his first in-person briefing since taking charge as chief executive in August, Walsh said IndiGo expected to begin receiving wide-body Airbus A350 aircraft from the second quarter of 2028.He said the airline had all the necessary ingredients to succeed in the long-haul market."We see incredible opportunities," Walsh said, while acknowledging the difficult operating environment for airlines.The industry is facing pressure from higher fuel costs, which have affected airline profitability. IndiGo reported a net loss of Rs 1,879.1 crore in the July-September quarter, with elevated fuel expenses and rupee depreciation weighing on its financial performance."The situation is challenging for the industry and we will continue to navigate through the challenges," Walsh said.The airline has also reduced capacity in response to the operating pressures. In the September quarter, its fuel expenses rose to Rs 9,966.8 crore, an increase of 67.2% from Rs 5,961.8 crore in the corresponding period last year.IndiGo's capacity, measured in available seat kilometres, declined 1% to 40.8 billion during the quarter.Despite a 4.7% fall in passenger numbers to 2.7 crore, passenger ticket revenue increased 29.3% to Rs 20,652.2 crore, while the load factor declined 2.2 percentage points to 80.3%.Walsh had said last week that the airline expected elevated fuel costs to persist for some time and would continue exploring internal measures to offset the increase.The airline's September-quarter loss was its third consecutive quarterly loss, as per the earlier report. Its total income, however, rose 24% year-on-year to Rs 24,311.9 crore.On IndiGo's expansion plans, Walsh said the airline expected deliveries of its wide-body A350 aircraft to begin in the second quarter of 2028. He said the carrier was well placed to enter the long-haul market.Walsh also described the upcoming Navi Mumbai airport as a significant opportunity for the airline. He said IndiGo's decision to shift some of its international flights to the new airport had been taken in the airline's interest.IndiGo currently operates more than 2,100 flights daily and has an operational fleet of over 400 aircraft.As of September 30, the airline had a fleet of 442 aircraft and operated a peak of 2,020 daily flights during the July-September quarter, including non-scheduled services.The airline's cash balance stood at Rs 52,685.4 crore at the end of September, comprising Rs 39,929 crore in free cash and Rs 12,756.4 crore in restricted cash. Its total debt, including capitalised operating lease liabilities, was Rs 87,303.1 crore, the report said.
Article Summary: IndiGo sees significant growth opportunities despite rising fuel costs and other pressures facing the aviation industry. CEO Willie Walsh said the airline would focus on maintaining a competitive cost base while navigating the challenges. IndiGo expected to begin receiving wide-body Airbus A350 aircraft from the second quarter of 2028.

The bottom line

sona-chandi

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market and other asset classes given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

With Diwali around the corner, gold and silver prices have brought an early surprise for consumers. After a dazzling rally that took both metals to record highs earlier this year, prices have cooled off, giving festive buyers a potential window to make their purchases.And the timing couldn't be better! For Indian households, Dhanteras shopping has never been just about chasing a good deal. Buying sona-chandi is a generations-old tradition, deeply rooted in the belief that precious metals bring prosperity, good fortune and a little extra sparkle to the year ahead.But before you rush to the jewellery store, there's a catch.The metals have been on a roller-coaster ride, and with prices fluctuating sharply, buyers are now faced with a dilemma:Should you buy now, or wait for another dip? Is gold the safer bet, or does silver offer better value?After a spectacular rally that took both metals to record highs on January 29, 2026, gold and silver prices have come crashing down, with silver taking the bigger hit.Gold, which touched Rs 1,75,231 per 10 grams, has slipped almost to below Rs 1.5 lakh levels. Silver, which soared to Rs 3,84,632 per kg, has lost nearly half its value and is now hovering around Rs 2 lakh per kg.Internationally too, the yellow metal has faced pressure around $4,000 per ounce, while silver has witnessed sharp swings around $50 per ounce.But what's behind the sudden fall?For starters, investors began booking profits after the record-breaking rally, putting downward pressure on both metals. Adding to the pressure, the US-Iran war pushed crude oil above $120 per barrel, fuelling inflation fears and concerns that the US Federal Reserve could keep interest rates higher for longer. Higher rates make non-interest-paying assets like gold and silver less attractive than bonds.Together, profit booking, higher yields and a stronger dollar have weighed on precious metal prices despite ongoing geopolitical tensions.Gold and silver have lost some of their shine lately, but is the worst behind us, or is there more drama ahead?According to Vedika Narvekar, research analyst of commodities & currencies at Anand Rathi Shares & Stock Brokers, both metals could face a few more bumps in the short term, but things may look brighter down the road.The gold could remain under pressure over the next one to two months too. The Fed's hawkish stance, inflation around 3.7% and Brent crude above $110 per barrel have raised concerns over further monetary tightening. US treasury yields near 5% and the dollar index around 102 could add to the pressure.Narvekar expects gold to trade between $3,950 and $4,200 per ounce internationally, or Rs 1,40,600–Rs 1,48,500 on the MCX."We see international gold trading in the $3,950–4,200/oz range (MCX Rs 1,40,600-Rs 1,48,500), with downside risk towards $3,800 (MCX Rs1,35,000) if oil prices remain elevated and rate expectations harden," she told TOI.However, ETF inflows of around $10 billion in September and continued central bank buying could cushion a deeper fall.In the long-term, Narvekar remains bullish, targeting $4,900 per ounce, or around Rs 1.75 lakh on the MCX, by the end of 2027. Central bank diversification, rising US debt, fiscal concerns and possible future interest-rate cuts could support prices."A sustained recovery will require softer bond yields and a weaker dollar; until then, expect volatility rather than a quick return to record highs," she added.Silver could face an even tougher road. Unlike gold, it isn't just an investment; it's also widely used in industries such as solar energy and electronics. That makes prices more sensitive to industrial demand, particularly as solar-panel manufacturers look to reduce silver usage.Narvekar expects silver to test $48–50 per ounce internationally, or Rs 1.70–1.80 lakh per kg on the MCX, amid elevated oil prices, rising yields and the Fed's hawkish stance.A gradual recovery towards $70 per ounce is possible in 2027, supported by electrification, electronics, data-centre demand and limited mine-supply growth. However, a return to January's peak of around $122 per ounce, or Rs 4.2 lakh per kg, appears unlikely."However, weaker solar demand, substitution and the possibility of a smaller market deficit could limit gains," Narvekar said.For investors, she advised caution rather than chasing a quick rebound."Investors should therefore treat silver as a higher-risk, higher-volatility holding than gold and accumulate in stages rather than expect a rapid return to peak levels," she said.With buying gold and silver being a Dhanteras tradition, the recent fall in prices may come as good news for shoppers, especially as precious metals have consistently delivered double-digit returns through bull and even bear markets.But is it better to buy now or wait a little longer?Experts explain how to time your purchase, what to keep in mind and how much of your money to put into precious metals.Trying to time the market can be tricky, but waiting for a bigger dip could also mean missing an opportunity.Ayush Verma, director of Annapurna Jewellers Pvt. Ltd, Varanasi, said, “While precious metal prices may witness further short-term fluctuations, predicting the exact market bottom is difficult.”Buyers should prioritise affordability, financial needs and investment horizons instead of waiting indefinitely.Adhil Shetty, CEO of BankBazaar, views the correction as a natural pause after a sharp rally rather than a sign of a bigger crash. With research reports pointing to higher prices over the coming year, waiting for a steep fall carries risks.“Buying in moderation, rather than trying to time the exact bottom, tends to serve festive buyers better over time,” he said.For those buying purely for investment, Hetal Vakil Valia, jewellery educator, designer and consultant, suggests a measured approach.“Consider investing around 40% to 50% of your planned budget during Dhanteras and keeping the rest liquid,” she said.This allows investors to spread purchases over the coming months and potentially benefit from further dips instead of committing their entire budget at one price.For many, Dhanteras purchases are driven by tradition and sentiment rather than investment returns.Valia believes that the correction offers a more comfortable entry point for festive buyers compared with earlier record highs.Verma also recommends that those buying jewellery or coins for the occasion focus on affordability and personal requirements rather than chasing the lowest price.In short, investors may prefer buying gradually, while festive shoppers can prioritise their needs and budget.With precious metals getting cheaper, filling your Dhanteras shopping basket might seem tempting. But from choosing the right metal to deciding between jewellery, coins, bars and ETFs, there's more to consider than the price tag.If protecting wealth is your priority, gold may be the better bet. It's generally considered relatively stable for long-term wealth preservation and diversification.Valia added, “If you are comfortable taking on more risk in pursuit of higher returns, silver is worth considering.”But then, why choose just one?“A balanced approach could involve gold as the core precious metal holding, complemented by a smaller silver allocation for diversification,” Verma told TOI.This could combine gold's relative stability with silver's growth potential while limiting exposure to the more volatile metal.Buying precious metals doesn't necessarily mean buying jewellery. For those investing purely for returns, coins and bars may be more cost-effective.Shetty said, “Coins and bars work out cheaper than jewellery once making charges and resale cuts are counted in, making them the better route for pure investment.”Valia points out that making charges can range from 10% to 20%, affecting resale returns.Jewellery, however, offers value beyond its price tag, from craftsmanship and heritage to gifting and personal enjoyment.So, while jewellery may suit festive and personal purchases, coins and bars could make more sense for investment-led buyers.Don't want the hassle of storing precious metals? ETFs let you invest in gold or silver without holding them physically, while electronic gold receipts give you ownership of gold stored in approved vaults.“Gold and silver ETFs skip storage and purity concerns altogether, and suit buyers who want exposure without holding the physical metal,” Shetty said.However, investors should compare brokerage, fund expenses, liquidity and market risks.And while ETFs and electronic gold receipts are regulated by SEBI, not every digital gold product has the same regulatory oversight.If jewellery is on your shopping list, look beyond the glitter!Verma advises checking design, purity, hallmarking and transparent making charges before purchasing.Remember, the quoted gold rate isn't necessarily the final bill. Making charges and other applicable costs can add to your expenses, while resale terms can affect how much you recover later.Those buying coins and bars should also compare purchase costs and resale options.Afterall, not every Dhanteras purchase needs to be an investment! Jewellery may be bought for wearing, gifting or passing down through generations, while investment purchases focus on potential returns.As Shetty explained, “Which metal makes more sense usually depends on the buyer's purpose rather than one being clearly ahead.”Ultimately, the right choice depends on whether you're shopping for tradition, enjoyment or long-term returns.Gold and silver can add some shine to your investment portfolio, but going overboard may not be the smartest move. And when it comes to the ideal amount to invest, experts have different takes.Verma recommends keeping around 5–15% of an investment portfolio in precious metals, depending on financial goals, risk appetite and existing holdings.Shetty suggests a more conservative benchmark. “Many financial planners suggest keeping gold in the 5% to 10% range, as a broad rule of thumb that varies by household,” he said.Valia recommends allocating 10–25% of total household savings to precious metals, depending on individual circumstances, with gold forming the larger share.“I would generally favour a 70:30 or 80:20 split between gold and silver, keeping gold as the larger component because of its relatively stable role in wealth preservation,” Valia said.However, precious metals should complement, not replace, investments such as equities, bonds, fixed deposits and cash reserves.Whether you're buying for tradition or investment, don't let the festive glitter outshine financial sense.Rather than chasing the perfect price, experts suggest spreading your purchases over time. As Shetty puts it, “Buying a little at a time helps smooth out price swings instead of committing it all at once.”If you're bringing home physical gold or silver, look beyond the price tag. Check purity, hallmarking, making charges and buyback terms.Prefer ETFs? Keep an eye on fees, market risks and regulatory safeguards. Avoid borrowing to invest!After all, while precious metals may help protect your wealth, they don't earn interest or dividends. So, before splurging on that festive sparkle, make sure your emergency savings, insurance and essential financial goals are taken care of.A littlecan certainly add shine to your portfolio, just make sure it doesn't eat up all your savings!
Article Summary: Gold, which touched Rs 1,75,231 per 10 grams, has slipped almost to below Rs 1.5 lakh levels. Silver, which soared to Rs 3,84,632 per kg, has lost nearly half its value. Investors began booking profits after the record-breaking rally, putting downward pressure on both metals.

Article Title: What will Trump losing US midterm elections mean for Sensex, Nifty? Explained
Article Text:
Experts believe that a strong win by Democrats would be a short-term positive for Indian stock markets. (Image for representative purpose only)

What US mid-terms mean for India’s stock market

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Investors are closely watching the US midterm elections for indications of whether the outcome could help reduce geopolitical uncertainty worldwide, an important factor shaping the outlook for equity markets.The polls decide which party holds control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate for the final two years of President Donald Trump 's term and the results pouring in at this moment hint at a possible victory for Democrats in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.Indian equities are already contending with a range of domestic market pressures. Uncertainty surrounding Donald Trump's tariff decisions, higher crude oil prices and bond yields, along with sustained foreign institutional investor (FII) selling, has pushed the Sensex and Nifty down.In this environment, investors are watching the US midterm elections for clues about their possible impact on global financial markets.Experts believe that a strong win by Democrats would be a short-term positive for Indian stock markets, though in the long-term global factors such as crude oil prices and quarterly results will continue to shape sentiment.VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geohit Investments Limited told TOI, “US mid-terms are unlikely to impact the Indian stock market significantly, whatever be the outcome.“The most likely scenario is the Democrats winning a majority in the House of Representatives. This will curtail the powers of President Trump especially on issues like tariffs. If the Democrats win both the house and the Senate, Trump will become a lame duck president. This can impact the US markets particularly the tech stocks, which, in turn, may prove beneficial for India which is widely regarded as a counter AI trade,” he said.“Indian market trend, going forward will be influenced by crude prices, FII flows and domestic macros,” he added.Somil Mehta, Head of Retail Research, Mirae Asset Sharekhan also believes that the US midterm elections could create some short-term volatility in Indian markets, but the outcome is unlikely to change the long-term market direction on its own.“If Democrats gain control of Congress, greater political checks on President Trump could limit policy changes and provide some stability to global markets. A divided Congress may also reduce uncertainty around aggressive policy decisions,” he told TOI.“For Indian markets, the bigger factors will remain crude oil prices, US bond yields, the dollar, FII flows and corporate earnings,” he said.Historical trends suggest that the Nifty has delivered its strongest gains over one-month, three-month and six-month periods following US midterm elections.An analysis by ET of the seven midterm elections held since 1998 shows that the Nifty recorded gains in five instances over each of these three periods.Madhavi Arora, chief economist at Emkay Global Financial Services, said a Congress controlled by Democrats could limit Trump's actions through legislative oversight. However, he would continue to exercise considerable authority over tariffs, immigration and foreign policy."Fiscal policy is likely to remain expansionary under either outcome, putting a floor under US bond yields," she said. Arora also warned that the Iran conflict could intensify again after the midterm elections, regardless of which party emerges ahead.The consequences for India are expected to be felt more through geopolitical developments than through any direct market impact, according to Emkay Research.Emkay Research also warned that a renewed escalation of the Iran conflict after the midterm elections could continue to put pressure on India's balance of payments, foreign exchange market and equities.On the global front, a strong Democratic win could challenge future fiscal negotiations and in turn curtail Trump’s deficit expanding plans – a positive for the bond market, says HDFC Bank.“On the other hand, it could also lead to an increase in regulatory scrutiny of the technology sector, with implications for the dollar and risk appetite.A democrat sweep is likely to be positive for bond yields and weigh on the US dollar. This was already visible in early morning trade with the Dollar Index marginally weaker at 101.37, while the US 10Y Treasury yield moderated close to 4.90%,” the bank said in a note.“If the market is surprised by the extent of the democratic win (number of seats won), we could see further reaction in the market, which could favour other DM currencies against the dollar. However, we expect any election related movements/volatility to be short-lived and attention to once again turn towards middle east tensions, AI trade and the rate hike narrative post this phase,” it added.
Article Summary: Polls decide which party holds control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate for the final two years of President Donald Trump's term. Experts believe that a strong win by Democrats would be a short-term positive for Indian stock markets, though in the long-term global factors such as crude oil prices and quarterly results will continue to shape sentiment.

Article Title: Gold prices may have crashed globally but gold smuggling in India has jumped to 50 tonnes from 3 tonnes in a year as 15% import duty widens the price gap; demand remains 29% lower year-on-year
Article Text:
The increase in import duty has changed the cost dynamics of gold supply in India. (Image for representative purpose only)

Gold smuggling up

India, the world’s second-largest gold market, is seeing a significant change in the way gold enters the country. The increase in import duty from 6% to 15% has made official imports more expensive, prompting a sharp rise in unofficial supplies. At the same time, record gold prices are putting pressure on consumer demand.According to a World Gold Council report, gold smuggling is estimated to have climbed to around 50 tonnes in the September quarter, compared with just three tonnes in the same period a year earlier. The surge highlights how higher import costs have had unintended consequences for the market.Gold demand recovered 24% sequentially to 162 tonnes in the previous quarter, supported largely by seasonal jewellery purchases. However, demand remained 29% below its year-ago level, as high prices continued to deter many buyers.Spending patterns told a different story. In the first nine months of the year, expenditure on gold increased 3% year-on-year and 38% sequentially, suggesting that consumers are spending more even though they are purchasing smaller quantities.Jewellery accounted for much of the quarterly recovery, with demand rising 33% sequentially to 100 tonnes.Seasonal buying and some easing in prices towards the end of the quarter helped support purchases.Despite this improvement, jewellery volumes remained 20% lower than a year earlier in the quarter. Demand over the first nine months was also down 18%, underlining the growing difficulty consumers face in affording gold at current prices.Investment demand, too, showed signs of stabilising after the strong buying seen last year. Demand for bars and coins increased 9% sequentially to 55 tonnes, although it was 40% lower year-on-year, partly reflecting the particularly strong comparison base. Gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs) also attracted greater interest, with demand rising to 5.3 tonnes in Q3 from 3.6 tonnes in the preceding quarter.The increase in import duty has changed the cost dynamics of gold supply in India. With the duty now at 15%, bringing gold into the country through official channels has become more expensive. This, in line with historical trends, has increased the incentive to use unofficial supply routes, according to an ET report.Looking ahead, festive-season purchases and demand during the wedding season are expected to provide support to the gold market in the December quarter. However, high prices could continue to weigh on jewellery volumes. Investment demand, meanwhile, is likely to depend largely on price movements and investors’ expectations of further gains.The market is therefore expected to witness a growing gap between the value of gold purchases and the quantity bought. Consumers may continue to spend more on gold, even as elevated prices limit the volume they can afford.
Article Summary: India, the world’s second-largest gold market, is seeing a significant change in the way gold enters the country. The increase in import duty from 6% to 15% has made official imports more expensive. At the same time, record gold prices are putting pressure on consumer demand.

Article Title: Midterm blues: Why a 'lame' duck Donald Trump may push for a quick India-US trade deal
Article Text:
Both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism. (Image for representative purpose only)

What this means for India-US trade deal

What does Democrats’ win in US midterm elections mean for India-US trade deal prospects? Will Donald Trump be forced to change his strategy?The unfavourable midterm election outcome is unlikely to prompt President Donald Trump to change course on trade, according to an analysis by Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI).But, it’s important to note that both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing and the strengthening of supply chains.Democratic lawmakers, too, favour protective tariffs to safeguard unionised workers and local industries.“The adverse midterm results won’t change President Donald Trump’s trade direction because both Democrats and Republicans now favor economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing, and strong supply chains,” says Ajay Srivastava, founder of GTRI.Unable to rely on Congress for every measure, Trump is expected to continue exercising powers already available to the administration. These include Sections 232 and 301, along with executive orders, Treasury sanctions and rules issued by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), to exert unilateral pressure on trading partners.According to GTRI, with foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win.“Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout,” he says.For several months, leaders on both sides have indicated that a trade agreement is close to being finalised. However, the lack of clarity over the US offer appears to have held up its completion, the think tank says.Trump is now likely to use his executive authority to push India towards an early agreement that opens up the Indian market to American agricultural and industrial products, while securing other significant concessions for US businesses.The agreement under negotiation between India and the US is fundamentally different from the other free trade agreements (FTAs) India has entered into. Under conventional trade agreements, both participating countries reduce or eliminate their regular import duties, which are governed by World Trade Organization (WTO) rules and referred to as Most Favoured Nation (MFN) tariffs.The proposed US–India framework, however, follows a different approach. Washington would continue to levy its regular MFN duties, while India would be required to eliminate or lower such tariffs on most industrial products and a wide range of agricultural goods.The February 6 US–India Joint Statement sets out further commitments for India. These include aligning its security and economic policies with Washington, purchasing $500 billion worth of American goods over five years, and relaxing domestic regulatory oversight of imports from the US.“The US may be relying on the threat of additional tariffs to secure India's compliance. These include potential measures linked to India's purchases of Russian oil under the Graham Act and Section 301,” Srivastava notes.Also, signing the agreement would not necessarily protect India from further tariff action. The US could still impose additional duties of 15% to 18% over and above its standard MFN rates. In effect, the proposed arrangement would amount to economic coercion.“India should not mistake relief from threatened tariffs for a balanced trade agreement. Opening its markets, committing to large purchases and limiting its policy choices would carry lasting costs, while any U.S. tariff relief could prove temporary. New Delhi should insist on clear, enforceable reciprocal concessions, consistency with WTO rules and full freedom to protect its energy security and development priorities. The pressure to announce a deal must not outweigh the need to secure one that serves India’s long-term interests,” Srivastava says.
Article Summary: Both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism. The US could still impose additional duties of 15% to 18% over and above its standard MFN rates. In effect, the proposed arrangement would amount to economic coercion. India should not mistake relief from threatened tariffs for a balanced trade agreement.

Article Title: IRDAI directs insurers to offer four-layer motor cover in compliance with SC order
Article Text:
Representative image

MUMBAI: IRDAI has operationalised the Supreme Court's directive to restructure motor insurance into four distinct sections, separating mandatory third-party liability and owner-driver personal accident cover from optional occupant liability, additional personal accident and own-damage covers. The new framework, which comes into force on Dec 15, 2026, seeks to make customers aware of what they are buying, what they are not buying and how much each component costs, without changing the basic covers available under existing policies.The circular translates the court's order in the case of National Insurance Company vs Thungala Dhana Laxmi into mandatory requirements for general insurers. The court had directed IRDAI, in consultation with the General Insurance Council and insurers, to introduce a four-layer structure for private cars and two-wheelers to help vehicle owners make informed choices.Under the framework, third-party liability remains mandatory. Legal liability to occupants or pillion riders, including employees of the insured, is optional. Personal accident cover for the owner-insured is mandatory, while cover for occupants, pillion riders and drivers other than the owner-driver is optional. Own-damage cover for the insured vehicle is also optional.To ensure uniformity across insurers, IRDAI has prescribed standard policy wordings based on drafts submitted by the General Insurance Council in consultation with the industry.Insurers must adopt these wordings and obtain a duly completed customer option form for every policy issued for a private car or two-wheeler. The form must record the covers selected by the customer and form part of the policy.The circular also requires insurers to issue a Customer Information Sheet at the point of sale and provide the option form for customers to select additional covers through online or offline channels. The policy schedule must separately disclose the actual coverage and premium charged under each section. The certificate of insurance must comply with the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.These requirements are intended to establish a documentary record of customer choices and make the cost of individual covers transparent, reducing ambiguity over whether a particular risk is insured.The framework also allows existing third-party policyholders to add legal liability cover for occupants during the policy period by paying an additional premium. This option must be exercised with the insurer that issued the third-party policy. The additional risk will commence from the date and time specified in the endorsement. Customers will not have to cancel their existing third-party policies to obtain the additional cover.While standardising the basic structure and policy wordings, IRDAI has allowed insurers to determine the pricing of own-damage covers in line with market conditions and continue to innovate on coverage. Insurers can also add or remove general exclusions and conditions based on the cover selected, provided they do not restrict the basic coverage prescribed under the four-layer structure.The circular also requires insurers to integrate the new structure with Bima Sugam by Dec 15, 2026, ensuring that the policies are available on the digital insurance marketplace from the date of implementation.The framework does not make all four sections compulsory. Third-party liability and the specified owner-insured personal accident cover remain mandatory, while occupant liability, additional personal accident cover and own-damage protection remain optional. Its central objective is to ensure that customers understand the coverage available and make a documented choice, backed by standardised policy terms and separate disclosure of premiums.
Article Summary: IRDAI has operationalised the Supreme Court's directive to restructure motor insurance. The new framework comes into force on Dec 15, 2026. It seeks to make customers aware of what they are buying and how much each component costs, without changing the basic covers available under existing policies.

Article Title: Gaana, Noise join hands for cobranded buds
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Noise and Gaana have announced the launch of the Noise Buds R1 (Gaana Edition), a co-branded product that brings together audio technology and music streaming in one offering.Priced at Rs 1,399, the earbuds come with a one-year Gaana Plus subscription. Article Title: Software freelancers get relief on export paperwork
Article Text: MUMBAI: RBI has eased export documentation requirements for individual software freelancers and other gig workers receiving payments from overseas clients by allowing information furnished to banks for crediting foreign currency earnings to serve as an Export Declaration Form (EDF). For other exporters, including companies, the deemed-submission facility is available only when the value of the inward remittance for the service does not exceed Rs 10 lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency.The change removes the need for resident individuals and low-value exporters to make a separate export declaration for each inward remittance. The amendment, notified on Nov 2, is effective retrospectively from Oct 1, 2026.Under the Fema export framework, payments received by freelancers from overseas clients are treated as export earnings rather than personal foreign remittances. These transactions have to be accounted for under the export declaration framework.
Article Summary: The change removes the need for resident individuals and low-value exporters to make a separate export declaration for each inward remittance. The amendment, notified on Nov 2, is effective retrospectively from Oct 1, 2026. Under the Fema export framework, payments received by freelancers from overseas clients are treated as export earnings.

Article Title: LTCG tax abolition may cost Rs 40k-50k crore
Article Text:
LTCG tax

NEW DELHI: Government could abolish long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax across investor categories even keeping its fiscal consolidation road map largely unaffected, as the resulting revenue loss is likely to be limited to Rs 40,000-50,000 crore in FY28, a report said on Tuesday.The report from SBI Research estimated that eliminating LTCG tax would reduce govt revenue by nearly 0.1-0.2% of GDP, a level it said could be absorbed while keeping fiscal deficit targets broadly on track. "We believe govt would be able to take this hit if hypothetically, the entire capital gains taxes were abolished," the report said. It estimated LTCG collections at around Rs 1 lakh crore in FY26 and projected them to decline to Rs 40,000-50,000 crore in FY27.
Article Summary: Government could abolish long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax across investor categories. The resulting revenue loss is likely to be limited to Rs 40,000-50,000 crore in FY28, a report said. SBI Research estimated that eliminating LTCG tax would reduce govt revenue by nearly 0.1-0.2% of GDP.

Article Title: TaMo looks at manufacturing Iveco in India
Article Text:
N Chandrasekaran

MUMBAI: N Chandrasekaran , who became chair of Iveco following Tata Motors ' biggest acquisition, said the combined ₹21 billion commercial vehicle group expects volumes, revenues and margins to grow over the next five years, as both companies explore opportunities to expand in each other's markets, including manufacturing Iveco products in India.Speaking in Turin, Chandrasekaran said the combination brings together complementary product portfolios and geographic footprints, uniting two profitable and cash-generative businesses with operations spanning India, Europe and Latin America.The acquisition, Tata Motors' biggest since its purchase of Jaguar Land Rover in 2008, has created the world's fourth-largest commercial vehicle manufacturer in the trucks-above-six-tonnes segment, with annual sales of nearly six lakh vehicles.The combined group operates in more than 130 countries, with 27 manufacturing plants, 25 research and development centres and over 73,000 employees.Tata Motors completed the initial settlement of its tender offer last week, securing nearly 90% stake in Iveco for about ₹4 billion and making the Italian truckmaker an indirect subsidiary. Tata Motors is also working on the delisting of Iveco, although Chandrasekaran declined to provide a timeline.Despite the combination, Iveco will continue to operate from its headquarters in Turin, he said.At the press conference, Tata Motors MD Girish Wagh, who has joined the Iveco board as a non-executive director, recalled the Indian company's long-standing association with the Italian city. "When Ratan Tata (former Tata Motors chairman) wanted to manufacture cars, he had turned to Turin," Wagh said.Iveco's existing brands, industrial operations and organisational identities will be preserved, while Tata Motors will support Iveco's current strategic and investment plans. Iveco CEO Olof Persson will remain in his role.
Article Summary: Tata Motors completed the initial settlement of its tender offer last week, securing nearly 90% stake in Iveco for about ₹4 billion. Tata Motors is also working on the delisting of Ive co, although Chandrasekaran declined to provide a timeline. The acquisition has created the world's fourth-largest commercial vehicle manufacturer.

Article Title: SBI net rises 14% to 23k crore, shares slip 1.8%
Article Text:
State Bank of India

MUMBAI: State Bank of India's Q2FY27 net profit rose 14.3% to Rs 23,038 crore, driven by a 14.7% increase in net interest income to Rs 49,143 crore and lower loan loss provisions. Net interest margin improved to 3.1% from just over 3% a year ago, while loan loss provisions fell 33% to Rs 2,759 crore as asset quality improved.However, the bank's shares fell 1.8% to Rs 969 as investors were disappointed with the 7.3% growth in operating profit to Rs 34,226 crore. The increase was held back by a 24% decline in other income to Rs 11,777 crore.Addressing newspersons, SBI chairman CS Setty reiterated the bank's guidance of 10-11% deposit growth and 14-15% credit growth. The bank has a corporate loan pipeline of Rs 7.8 lakh crore, he said."If nominal GDP growth is around 12 to 12.5%, normally the SBI credit growth rate is 3 to 4% over that and that is where the guidance of 14 to 15% is coming from," explained Setty.The bank does not face any immediate compulsion to raise deposit rates, given its comfortable liquidity position. SBI had excess statutory liquidity ratio (SLR) holdings of more than Rs 4 lakh crore as of Sept 30, providing adequate headroom to fund credit growth, he said.
Article Summary: State Bank of India's Q2FY27 net profit rose 14.3% to Rs 23,038 crore. Net interest margin improved to 3.1% from just over 3% a year ago. The bank has a corporate loan pipeline of Rs 7.8 lakh crore, he said.

Article Title: Won't open up dairy sector or let in genetically modified products: Piyush Goyal
Article Text:
Goyal says India will not open its dairy sector in trade deals or allow imports of genetically modified products, calling them sensitive issues for farmers and religious sentiments

NEW DELHI: With India, US close to finalising a trade, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal Tuesday said India has never opened up its dairy sector in any free trade agreement and will not allow imports of genetically modified products, describing both as "very sensitive" issues for the country.Addressing students of Kirori Mal College, Goyal said India has "never ever" compromised on any sensitive item and has always protected its farmers, fishermen, and MSMEs in trade pacts."We are sensitive to opening up to certain agricultural produce, certain goods that we are very strong on like marine products. We are very sensitive to opening our dairy. In fact, till date, we have never opened up dairy for anybody. We are very sensitive not to allow any genetically modified products to come to India and we have never allowed it and we'll never allow it in the future," he said.He said, "We are sensitive to our religious sensitivities. So very often in foreign countries, they use calf meat or Rennet while producing their dairy products. We don't allow that in India. It is strictly got to be certified... so that religious sensitivities of the large parts of India are not hurt."Rennet is an enzyme used in cheese-making, traditionally obtained from the stomach lining of young calves. PTI
Article Summary: Piyush Goyal says India will not open its dairy sector in trade deals or allow imports of genetically modified products. Goyal: India has "never ever" compromised on any sensitive item and has always protected its farmers, fishermen, and MSMEs in trade pacts.

Article Title: Industry bodies debate LTCG pitch ahead of pre-budget discussions
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Ahead of the pre-budget consultation with revenue secretary Arvind Shrivastava on Wednesday, industry bodies were working out their final wish list on long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) - the most-discussed budgetary proposal this year.Executives at industry associations said that there were competing views from members and tax experts and a final call on how the demand should be worded was yet to be taken. While the proposal is not completely new, it has got a major thrust amid stagnant stock market indices and negative returns for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) due to a weak rupee. The call gained further momentum after the Centre scrapped the 12.5% long-term capital gains tax on FPI investment in govt securities in June as part of a strategy to support the rupee.On Tuesday, while some of the bodies were finetuning their position, most strident were FPIs, demanding that govt abolish the tax at least for them. There are some supporters of this among industry representatives as well. But politically, especially with mutual funds and retail investors emerging as a large investor community, it may not be possible for govt to only focus on overseas investors and ignore the claims of domestic investors -- more so, when complaints about high GST and personal income tax rates have just subsided.With revenue impact being a concern, there is some discussion around a graded reduction in LTCG. So, some industry representatives have suggested that short-term capital gains tax and securities transaction tax (STT) be retained in their current form and LTCG in year 1 also be left unchanged at 12.5%. But those who hold the shares longer should be charged concessional LTCG, which could fall to zero over three-five years.There is also a school of thought that STT should be abolished and LTCG be retained. Then, there are suggestions that STT should apply to F&O but be removed for the cash segment.There is also a section which believes that FPIs will come once stock market valuations correct further and the rupee stabilises.As finance minister has said in her public statements, she is keeping track of the debate. The outcome will be known only on Feb 1 when she presents a record-equalling tenth budget.
Article Summary: Long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) is the most-discussed budgetary proposal this year. It has got a major thrust amid stagnant stock market indices and negative returns for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) The call gained further momentum after the Centre scrapped the 12.5% LTCG on FPI investment in govt securities in June.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $200 million investment faces high risk as Six Flags investigated for securities fraud amid tragic deaths
Article Text:
Travis Kelce's investment.(Image via Getty Images)

Travis Kelce’s investment at risk as Six Flags Entertainment faces questioning over securities fraud

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
